prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits via transformer/feeder bays. Automation boundary: bay monitoring/control, station coordination, external interfaces; primary equipment, protection and field wiring stay under approved designs.

Elements:
- Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): bay sequencing, status evaluation, permissive checks; produces Bay Status Digest; requests breaker operations from Breaker Control Unit only when mode/permissives allow.
- North Bay Controller, South Bay Controller: bay-specific automation.
- Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): detects feeder faults, initiates protection in its zone; produces Relay Diagnostic Note on self-monitoring conditions.
- Breaker Control Unit: executes authorized breaker operations; enforces local interlocks.
- Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): consolidated operator interface showing station/bay indications, operating conditions, communication quality (does not replace local indications); performs no protective functions; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip for recordkeeping.
- Station Gateway: authorized external connection boundary; carries supervisory communications between station functions and remote operations interfaces.
- Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): acquires satellite timing reference; distributes time over time-distribution network for consistent event timestamps; produces Clock Drift Snapshot when measured offset meets reporting condition; provides time-quality indications.
- Sequence Event Archive: retains event information.
- Engineering Workstation: controlled configuration/maintenance.
- Maintenance Remote Terminal: maintenance access only; not local operating authority.
- Station DC System: supplies control/operating power to automation and protection within capacity.

Actors:
- Control Room Operator: directs operation, verifies states, uses supervisory displays to assess and coordinate.
- Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): maintains settings, evaluates relays via change process.
- Substation Field Crew: field work under switching instructions/clearances.
- Substation Supervisor: oversees supervisory system use; escalates unresolved availability concerns.

Modes/requirements:
- Local control precedes remote when selected local; remote/supervisory commands subject to permissions, procedure, bay selection, interlocks, availability.
- Local interlocks/equipment logic authoritative for switching.
- Protection trips independent of bay control.
- Comms interruption may make displays stale/unavailable; after recovery operators confirm indications are current.
- Timing modes: synchronized, degraded, unavailable; on reference loss devices use own clock/holdover (degrades over time). Timestamps aid correlation, don't validate measurements/protection.
- Station power loss can interrupt supervisory visibility and time distribution until restored.

New part:
S052: The Feeder Protection Relay provides local protection for its assigned feeder and operates independently of supervisory control availability.
S053: Its approved setting group defines the pickup levels, time delays, and logic required for the feeder protection scheme.
S054: The Protection Relay Engineer develops setting changes against the approved protection study and the current equipment data.
S055: The Protection Relay Engineer documents the engineering basis and expected operational effect for each proposed change.
S056: Engineering Workstation maintains the working configuration under revision control.
S057: Engineering Workstation produces the Settings Review Receipt after a settings review is completed.
S058: Each proposed change receives a unique revision identifier before review begins.
S059: The Protection Relay Engineer verifies that proposed values agree with the approved coordination objectives.
S060: A second qualified reviewer independently checks calculations, logic changes, and device applicability.
S061: The review confirms that the proposed configuration is complete, internally consistent, and suitable for the intended feeder.
S062: Coordination checks consider upstream and downstream protection behavior across the expected operating range.
S063: Protection settings are not approved solely on the basis of copied values from another installation.
S064: Engineering Workstation retains the approved configuration and its revision history for controlled access.
S065: Configuration access is limited to personnel with assigned engineering responsibilities.
S066: The Protection Relay Engineer records the approval status before any setting change is released for implementation.
S067: Before deployment, the approved configuration is checked against the intended device model and firmware version.
S068: A controlled outage or other approved work window is required when implementation could affect feeder protection.
S069: The Substation Field Crew follows the authorized work instructions during device access and setting transfer.
S070: After installation, the implemented values are compared with the approved configuration.
S071: The Feeder Protection Relay is functionally checked to confirm the intended protection behavior after a change.
S072: Any discrepancy stops release of the configuration until its cause is resolved and reviewed.
S073: The Substation Supervisor ensures that engineering changes follow the established authorization and operational control process.
S074: The Substation Field Crew is known operationally as Cinder during field activities.
S075: Cinder performs inspections, maintenance, and switching support within the boundaries of approved work.
S076: Field access begins only after the required work authorization and site entry controls are confirmed.
S077: The Control Room Operator coordinates operational access with the Switching Desk Coordinator before work that could affect energized equipment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
